system.name: Teola
system.one_liner: an orchestration framework that optimizes LLM-based applications using primitive operations as the basic execution unit

components.name: Execution Engine Registry & Profile
components.role: developers register execution engines and their latency profiles in the offline stage

components.name: Optimization Strategies
components.role: developers optionally specify optimization strategies for certain primitive operations

components.name: Workflow Template
components.role: developers supply a template outlining the app's components and execution sequence

components.name: Frontend
components.role: accepts a declarative query (question, docs, chunk size, synthesis mode, etc.)

components.name: Graph Optimizer
components.role: builds a query-specific primitive-level dataflow graph and optimizes it into an execution plan (e-graph)

components.name: Runtime
components.role: schedules and executes the optimized graph online

components.name: Engine Scheduler
components.role: schedules primitive operations onto execution engine instances

components.name: Backend Engines
components.role: execution engine instances (e.g. GPU) that run primitive operations

components.name: Primitive Operations
components.role: basic units of execution scheduled and run by the runtime

flows.what: registered execution engines and latency profiles configure the deployed app
workflow template outlining app components and execution sequence
optimized execution graph (e-graph) built from primitive nodes

content.key_idea: Offline-registered engines, profiles and a workflow template let the online path compile each query into a primitive-level dataflow graph that is optimized into an e-graph before runtime scheduling and execution.
content.reading_order: Top-down: the dashed offline configuration row first, then step 1-4 arrows through the Frontend, Graph Optimizer, and Runtime, with a feedback arrow back to the Frontend.

evidence: Teola is a novel orchestration framework to optimize the execution of LLM-based applications with primitive operations as the basic unit
developers register execution engines for an app, such as those for embedding models, LLMs, and database operations
users can customize the workflow (Figure 5), allowing for parameter tuning of components

summary: This figure gives a system overview of Teola, an orchestration framework that optimizes LLM-based applications using primitive operations as the basic execution unit. In the offline stage (1), developers register execution engines with their latency profiles, optionally set optimization strategies, and supply a workflow template describing the app's components and execution order. In the online stage, an incoming declarative query (e.g., question, docs, chunk size, synthesis mode) enters the Frontend (2), which the Graph Optimizer turns into a query-specific, primitive-level dataflow graph and optimizes into an execution plan (an e-graph) (3). The Runtime then schedules and executes that graph across Backend Engine instances via its Graph Scheduler and Engine Scheduler, returning results back to the Frontend (4). Colored boxes distinguish the one-time offline configuration from the per-query online pipeline, with small example graphs illustrating how optimization passes restructure the primitive nodes.
summary_zh: 该图展示 Teola 系统概览：离线①注册执行引擎、优化策略与工作流模板；在线查询进入 Frontend②，Graph Optimizer 构建并优化图元级数据流图③，Runtime 调度后端引擎执行，结果④返回前端。
notes: The paper's title names the system 'Ayo' but the abstract, this figure's caption, and all body text around it call it 'Teola'; the name used here follows the figure/caption/text.
